213: Let $\Lambda=\Lambda(x_1,x_2,\ldots)$ be the ring of symmetric functions with integral coefficients. This space has a ${\mathbb Z}$-linear basis consisting of \emph{Schur functions} $s_{\lambda}$,
214: where $\lambda$ is an integer partition. Consider the ideal
215: \[I_{r,n-r} = \mathrm{Span}_\mathbb{Z}\left\{s_\lambda\mid \lambda\nsubseteq (n-r)^r \right\} \]
216: of $\Lambda$. Then one has the following standard presentation of the cohomology of Grassmannians:
217: \[H^*(\mathrm{Gr}_{r,n})\cong \Lambda/I_{r,n-r}. \]
218: We will use an overline to denote the projection $\Lambda\to\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}$. Specifically, we will write $\overline{\Lambda}$ as a shorthand for $\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}$. We will also distinguish between $s_{\lambda}\in \Lambda$, the usual Schur function, and $\overline{s}_{\lambda}$ for its image in $\overline{\Lambda}$.

claims.text: For \(v_{r,s,t,n}\), \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), and \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\); the lower family is indexed by \(i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 219-235]
Partition conjugation is a ring involution and sends \(I_{r,n-r}\) to \(I_{n-r,r}\). [source-2@L1756-L1772|claim=formal-document]

1756: \subsection{Proof of Theorem~\ref{J-generators}}
1757: \label{minconjsection}
1758:   The proof of the second statement will follow from the first, via the
1759: well-known ring involution $\omega$ on symmmetric functions defined by
1760: $$
1761: \begin{aligned}
1762: \Lambda &\overset{\omega}{\rightarrow} \Lambda \\
1763: s_\lambda &\longmapsto s_{\lambda'}
1764: \end{aligned}
1765: $$
1766: where $\lambda'$ is the conjugate partition to $\lambda$.  This means
1767: that $\omega$ sends the ideal $I_{r,n-r}$ to the ideal $I_{n-r,r}$.
1768: Hence the set \eqref{generating-set-two} generates $J_v$ within
1769: $\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}$, where $v$ corresponds to an $i \times j$
1770: rectangle, if and only if the set \eqref{generating-set-one} generates
1771: the ideal $J_{v^\prime}$ within $\Lambda/I_{n-r,r}$, where $v^\prime$
1772: corresponds to a $j\times i$ rectangle.

claims.text: Under \(r=j+c,\ q=i+p,\ i,j\ge1,\ p,c\ge0\), conjugation induces \(\Lambda/I_{q,r}\cong\Lambda/I_{r,q}\), transports the interval ideal and \(A_+J\), and sends the lower family for \((q,r,j,i,c,p)\) bijectively onto the right family for \((r,q,i,j,p,c)\).
